legend: You are given 2n%%ZSMJ0%% points, you need to pair them to create n%%ZSMJ1%% rectangles so that the intersection of all those rectangles forms a positive area. In how many ways you can do that? Find the number of ways modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ2%%.
Pairing two points (x1,y1%%ZSMJ3%%) and (x2,y2%%ZSMJ4%%) forms the rectangle with bottom-left corner (min(x1,x2),min(y1,y2)%%ZSMJ5%%) and top-right corner (max(x1,x2),max(y1,y2)%%ZSMJ6%%).
input: The first line of input contains a single integer T%%ZSMJ7%% (1≤T≤3200%%ZSMJ8%%), the number of test cases.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ9%% (1≤n≤105%%ZSMJ10%%), the number of rectangles you need to make.

The following 2n%%ZSMJ11%% lines each contains two space-separated integers xi,yi%%ZSMJ12%% (−109≤xi,yi≤109%%ZSMJ13%%), representing the coordinates of the ith%%ZSMJ14%% point. All points are distinct.
The sum of n%%ZSMJ15%% over all test cases doesn't exceed 5×105%%ZSMJ16%%.
output: For each test case output a single line with the number of ways to pair the 2n%%ZSMJ17%% points modulo 109+7%%ZSMJ18%%.
